habitat: Singly or in pairs in high and low-altitude evergreen forest and riverine woodland. More secretive than Karoo Thrush.
summary: A common resident. Dark olive-brown above, with a throat speckled black on white and orange underparts. The highveld race has a brown breast. The vent is white or dusky, the eye-ring is brown, and the bill and legs are orange-yellow. From the ground it calls a thin wheet. No Kemp estimate is stored.

similar.note: Karoo Thrush is duller, with little or no throat spotting, a greyish vent and an orange eye-ring. Only its underbelly is orange.

bill.shape: Orange-yellow, with a dark wedge on the culmen.

head.pattern: Throat speckled black on white. Dark olive-brown above.

underparts.pattern: Underparts orange. The highveld race has a brown breast. The vent is white or dusky.

viewNotes.note: Dark above and orange below, with an orange-yellow bill.
Throat speckled black on white. The eye-ring is brown.
Orange underparts. The vent is white or dusky.

calls.description: From the ground, a thin 'wheet'. From a tree in summer it has a variety of loud pleasant songs. The grade A call is from near Louis Trichardt. The filename is XC502734-2 O Thrush.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Olive-brown and orange-yellow are not stored as single colours. The highveld breast is brown, so the breast colour is not stored as one token. The grade A call is from Limpopo. No Kemp estimate is stored.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.
